queryIntent: Is Google Search down, or is the problem on my site?
intendedAudience: Site owners and search practitioners deciding which evidence to inspect first when they notice a change on their own site.
decision: Decide whether to check the official Google Search Status source for a current incident and separately gather own-site evidence, without treating a historical controlled record as a cause.

metadata.title: Is Google Search down, or is the problem on my site?
metadata.description: A source-bound three-step guide for checking official Google Search status, historical controlled examples, and your own-site evidence without making a causal claim.

sourceBindings.purpose: Official Google Search Status source to check directly at decision time.
Official Google Search Central source material for source-bound context.

factualStatements.text: The guide binds its current-status check to the admitted official Google Search Status endpoint.
The guide binds its Search Central context to the admitted official Google Search Central feed endpoint.
Search Receipt records are controlled historical examples rather than current incident evidence.

workflow.instruction: Check the admitted official Google Search Status source directly at decision time; record only what that source shows then.
Use Search Receipt only to inspect controlled historical examples and source-bound context; do not treat a matching record as current incident evidence.
Compare timing and observations from your own site evidence with the official source, and retain uncertainty when the comparison does not establish a connection.

boundaries.currentOfficialStatus: Check the official Google Search Status source directly at decision time. This guide does not report a current status or incident.
boundaries.historicalControlledExamples: Search Receipt records are controlled historical examples, not current incident evidence.
boundaries.ownSiteEvidence: Your own site evidence is separate from official status and controlled examples; your own site evidence comparison that does not establish a connection remains uncertain.
boundaries.noCausation: A matching record does not explain a change on your own site.
unknowns: This guide cannot determine whether Google Search is currently down.
This guide cannot establish the cause of a change on your own site.
This guide does not establish a connection when timing or observations do not support one.

faqs.question: Is Google Search down right now?
faqs.answer: Check the admitted official Google Search Status source directly at decision time. This guide does not state the source's present result.

faqs.question: Does a matching Search Receipt record explain my site's change?
faqs.answer: No. Records are controlled historical examples and do not establish the cause of a change on your own site.

faqs.question: What should I compare before investigating?
faqs.answer: Compare the official source observed at decision time with dated evidence from your own site, and retain uncertainty if the comparison does not establish a connection.

correctionAndCurrentnessPolicy: Check the official source directly at decision time because this guide does not carry current incident state. If a source binding or guide statement needs correction, correct the contract before any route proposal and preserve the boundary that it does not explain an own-site change.
